name: LT1057 / LT1058
tagline: Linear Tech's fast, precise JFET dual and quad. Chinese and Korean rollers call it cold, fast and resolving.

lineage.note: Original LTC datasheet code 10578f*. Introduction year unconfirmed.
Rehosts datasheet 10578fd; lt1057.html and lt1058.html product pages are live.

part_numbers.note: Dual, standard 8-pin pinout, PDIP and SO. ADI product page live.
8-pin PDIP. 'ACN' (Baidu Tieba) probably means A-grade LT1057ACN8; codes unconfirmed.
'Gold can' prized by HIFIDIY users. Codes LT1057ACH/CH/AMH unconfirmed; likely NOS only.
Quad, standard 14-pin pinout. ADI product page live.
0 °C to 70 °C grade beside LT1058AC / LT1058C; probably wide SO (unconfirmed).

key_specs.value: 14 V/µs typ, 10 V/µs min; settles 1.3 µs to 0.02%
50 pA (CN hobby sources quote about 60 pA)

reputation.summary: Praise comes mainly from Chinese and Korean op-amp rollers. Baidu Tieba's 40-op-amp roundup credits it with extension, speed and dynamics but a cool tone and slightly recessed mids. HIFIDIY users call the gold-can version resolving but 'cold' and roll it beside the OPA2111HK. EET-China, digipine and sounting.com echo this. All subjective.
typical_uses: DAC I/V and output stage rolling (DIY)
Headphone amp and preamp socket upgrades
caveats: Praise is regional (CN/KR forums) and subjective; no Western consensus found.
The 'cold' voicing may not suit systems that are already bright.
Metal-can versions are old or NOS stock, with counterfeit and remark risk.
JFET bias current rises with temperature (50 pA specified at 70 °C).

counterfeit_notes: No LT1057-specific fake reports known. Sought-after TO-5 and early DIP parts are NOS, sold via Taobao, eBay and brokers. Distrust cheap 'gold cans'; check marking, date codes, offset and bias current against the datasheet.
